BACKPORT: FROMLIST: cros_ec: handle MKBP more events flag CL:1341159 adds a "more events" flag to allow the EC to notify us that there are more MKBP events waiting to be served. This CL extends the cros_ec bottom-half IRQ handler to listen to that flag in order to try and serve all known events before returning to the kernel with IRQ_HANDLED. This serves an optimization purpose as it minimizes the round-trip back and forth from the interrupt handler, and it also improves the quality of sensor timestamping, as it avoids a mismatch of event times between EC and AP that can confuse the median filter we use in the sensor ring. As described in the EC CL, this change is forward and backward compatible. This would be a cherry-pick of CL:1340983, but the code structure is different enough between kernel versions 4.4 and 4.14 that several tweaks are required to make things compile and work. It has been sent upstream as https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/1019477/ BUG=b:119570064, b:112102925, b:114915792 TEST=verify that sensor events come in and have sensible values and timestamps I had to tweak the merge of cros_ec_proto, but it was straight forward. Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1358742 Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ie51c5074489d3f076a907da30762e2f604c0e6f1 Signed-off-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551940 Reviewed-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: mfd: cros_ec: check for NULL transfer function As new transfer mechanisms are added to the EC codebase, they may not support v2 of the EC protocol. If the v3 initial handshake transfer fails, the kernel will try and call cmd_xfer as a fallback. If v2 is not supported, cmd_xfer will be NULL, and the code will end up causing a kernel panic. Add a check for NULL before calling the transfer function, along with a helpful comment explaining how one might end up in this situation. Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> (from https://lkml.org/lkml/2019/4/3/1192) BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=no kernel crash when v3 only device loads Change-Id: I392db6a7657a5be0f74280ac852f14ec0cd3305c Signed-off-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1555214 Reviewed-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: cros_ec_istp loops until events are gone The ISH FW supports a flags that allows the kernel to continue to query for more MKBP events until they are all consumed. This is the preferred method for consuming events after receiving a MKBP event. Also record the timestamp as close to the hardware event as possible without breaking encapsulation boundaries. BRANCH=none BUG=b:129159505 TEST=AP is honoring flag and calling to get more events if needed Change-Id: Id8f433bc08ae5329502668b443da96eb26a8b099 Signed-off-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1555219 Reviewed-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mathew King <mathewk@chromium.org>

arc: Disallow running bootstrap commands with $PATH. android-sh sets up PATH to /sbin:/vendor/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin. Here /vendor/bin is prioritized over /system/bin, which makes some sense (though arguable), but on some boards (e.g. nocturne) there's /vendor/bin/sh, so running "sh" without absolute path executes one in /vendor/bin. It sets up PATH differently: localhost ~ # android-sh :/ # echo $PATH /sbin:/vendor/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin :/ # /system/bin/sh -c 'echo $PATH' /sbin:/vendor/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin :/ # /vendor/bin/sh -c 'echo $PATH' /vendor/bin:/vendor/xbin Thus some commands like logcat are not available: :/ # /vendor/bin/sh -c 'which logcat'; echo $? 1 This is tricky, so this change updates arc.BootstrapCommand to reject all commands without absolute paths. Note that this problem does not exist for adb shell: localhost ~ # adb shell 'echo $PATH; which sh' /sbin:/system/sbin:/system/bin:/system/xbin:/odm/bin:/vendor/bin:/vendor/xbin /system/bin/sh BUG=chromium:949853 TEST=tast run nocturne arc.Boot arc.BuildProperties arc.MiniContainer Change-Id: I5681398ed46a0daf542c9ff3c4d5531eb3bb27fe Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1554380 Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>

arc: Wait for logd to start before starting to save logcat. We sometimes see empty logcat.txt even for ARC test that ran several minutes. This happens when we start logcat too early; if we run logcat before logd is started, logcat exits immediately with writing an error message to stderr. To workaround this issue, poll "logcat -ds" before starting to save logcat to make sure logd is up. BUG=chromium:946981 TEST=android-sh -c 'setprop ctl.stop logd; logcat -ds; echo $?' TEST=tast run DUT arc.Boot # on nocturne Change-Id: Ie485adf22ebc9dbc3d1c2fd8848218ba96ffe546 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1552620 Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

edition: Use dyn syntax for trait objects Found by running: `cargo rustc -- -D bare_trait_objects` Bare trait objects like `&Trait` and `Box<Trait>` are soft-deprecated in 2018 edition and will start warning at some point. As part of this, I replaced `Box<Trait + 'static>` with `Box<dyn Trait>` because the 'static bound is implied for boxed trait objects.
